key_insight: The paper extends a known mathematical equivalence between two-dimensional vortical and capillary free-boundary problems to a new pair of problems: hollow vortices in shear/strain flow and bubbles with surface tension in straining flow.
engineering_relevance: This analogy can let researchers transfer solution methods and exact identities between apparently different fluid systems, improving analysis of free-surface and vortex-interface dynamics.
method: Construct an exact isolated solution for the special case γ = 0.
Compute numerical solutions for nonzero γ.
Use conformal mapping identities from capillary-flow theory and apply them to the hollow-vortex setting under parameter constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports one exact solution at γ = 0 and numerical solutions for nonzero γ, indicating the framework is validated across both analytic and computed cases.
watch_item: The equivalence appears to hold only under specific parameter constraints, so the analogy may not generalize to arbitrary flow configurations or geometries.
paper_title: Extension of a mathematical analogy between vortical flows without surface tension and irrotational capillary flows
